newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BANKS RISK TECHNOLOGY LAG -INSTITUTE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BANKS RISK TECHNOLOGY LAG -INSTITUTE.

text.p: After the banking crisis of the early 1990s, Finnish banks may have trouble finding funds to make the technology investments needed to compete globally, the Pellervo economic research institute said on Tuesday.

"Finnish banks may have trouble finding enough money for the information technology investments that are indispensible for banks to retain their competitive edge," the institute said in a statement announcing the results of a new study.
"Global competition and the rapid pace of technological development will in the future require banks to make enormous investments in information technology," it said.
Looking at other competitive challenges, the institute said Finnish banks would need to change their pricing of various services, deposits and credit.
Banks would have to change their pricing policy because customers of bank credit increasingly have investments as well as debt and want more comparable pricing, it said.

The institute said banks had strengthened their position in the financial market by breaking into business traditionally dominated by insurance companies as Finns increasingly seek new investment vehicles as alternatives to bank deposits.
"The banks' increasingly wealthy and aging clientele are looking for alternatives, for instance in various mutual funds," the institute said.

Many investment alternatives are already provided by banks or financial institutions belonging to banking groups, so the bank-centred character of the Finnish financial market may have even been accentuated in recent years, it said.
But, as households are unlikely to become direct investors in the stock market, they would continue to be the backbone of the banking industry in the future, the institute predicted.
